dashboard.label: Webex Bot Alerts
dashboard.description: Bring your own Webex bot: create a bot token + space, wire it into the lab, and send Splunk alerts to Webex.

html.h2: Send Splunk alerts to Webex — bring your own bot
html.p: This lab ships a custom "Webex message" alert action. It has no standing connection to Webex — when an alert fires, Splunk runs a small script that makes a single outbound HTTPS call to Webex using your credential. Everyone brings their own bot, so nothing sensitive is committed to the repo. Three steps: 1) create a bot, 2) create a space and get its room ID, 3) wire the credential into the lab. Then enable an alert and watch messages land in your space.

panel.title: 1 — Create a Webex bot (get the token)

ol.li: Go to developer.webex.com/my-apps/new/bot and sign in with your Webex account.
Fill in a Bot name, a unique Bot username (e.g. dcloud-splunk-bot → becomes dcloud-splunk-bot@webex.bot), pick an icon, add a description.
Copy the Bot access token shown on the next screen — this is shown only once. This is your WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN.

html.p: Bot tokens are long-lived (~100 years), unlike the 12-hour personal developer token — which is why a bot is the right choice for an unattended alert action. If you lose the token, open the bot under My Webex Apps and regenerate it.

panel.title: 2 — Create a space and get its room ID

ol.li: In the Webex app, create a space, e.g. "dCloud Alerts".
Add your bot to the space by its …@webex.bot username. A bot can only post to spaces it belongs to — this is the step people forget.

Get the space's ID: open the interactive List Rooms docs at developer.webex.com/docs/api/v1/rooms/list-rooms, paste your bot token as the bearer, run GET /v1/rooms, find your space by title, and copy its id. This is your WEBEX_ROOM_ID.

html.p: Prefer zero setup? A Webex Incoming Webhook gives you a single URL and needs no room ID — set WEBEX_WEBHOOK_URL instead of the token+room. Create one from a space: Apps ▸ Incoming Webhooks ▸ Add.

panel.title: 3 — Wire the credential into the lab

html.p: The credential lives out of the repo in $SPLUNK_HOME/var/lib/dcloud/webex.env. The easy path: pass it to apply.sh as env vars at session start and it writes the file for you.

p.b: Option A — bot token + room ID:

html.pre: sudo WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN='<your bot token>' \ WEBEX_ROOM_ID='<your room id>' \ bash /opt/dcloud-splunk/apply.sh
html.p: Or write the file directly (no re-run of apply.sh needed — the action reads it on each fire):
html.pre: sudo install -d -m700 -o splunk -g splunk /opt/splunk/var/lib/dcloud sudo -u splunk tee /opt/splunk/var/lib/dcloud/webex.env >/dev/null <<'EOF' WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN=<your bot token> WEBEX_ROOM_ID=<your room id> EOF sudo chmod 600 /opt/splunk/var/lib/dcloud/webex.env
html.p: The file is chmod 600 and owned by the splunk user. It is never committed and is wiped on session reset (re-run apply.sh with the env vars, or the dCloud startup command, to recreate it).

panel.title: Is a credential wired up? (recent send attempts)

search.query: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd "webex_notify:" | rex field=_raw "webex_notify:\s+(?<detail>.*)$" | eval Result=case(like(detail,"sent%"),"● sent", like(detail,"no Webex credential%"),"● no credential set", 1==1,"● error") | table _time Result detail | sort - _time

panel.title: Demo alerts using the Webex action

search.query: | rest /servicesNS/-/alerts/saved/searches | search action.webex_notify=1 | eval Enabled=if(disabled=0 AND is_scheduled=1,"● enabled","○ disabled") | rename title as Alert, cron_schedule as Schedule | table Alert Enabled Schedule action.webex_notify.param.message | rename action.webex_notify.param.message as "Message sent"

ol.li: Go to Settings ▸ Searches, reports, and alerts (in the Search & Reporting app), find "dcloud - SNMP trap received → Webex" or "dcloud - Service unavailable → Webex", and enable it (they ship disabled).
Or attach the action to any search: Save As ▸ Alert ▸ Add Actions ▸ Webex message, set the message, and run it.
Fire it (open the alert and click Run, or wait for its schedule). A message appears in your Webex space, and the send-attempts panel above turns green (sent (HTTP 200)).

html.p: Troubleshooting: yellow "no credential set" → webex.env is missing or empty (step 3). Red "error" → usually the bot isn't a member of the space (step 2), a bad token, or the room ID is wrong; the detail column shows the HTTP status from Webex. The lab must have outbound HTTPS to webexapis.com.
